solves: Gives a list the person picks from one option with its label and, when needed, a start, a helper text and the selected look, shared by the lists of nph-select and nph-combobox.
use_when: As a child of nph-select, one per option of the list.
With start=dot when each option has a state, written in the label.
With secondary when a helper text tells options with similar labels apart.
do_not_use_when: On its own, outside the list that owns it: it has no role there.
With a checkbox marker: multiple choice belongs to nph-multi-combobox.
Mixing options with and without a start in the same list: use one start.
With the status dot and no state written in the label.

slot.constraint: The label: the text of the option, already localized. It is the accessible name of the option and the text the trigger shows when it is chosen.

value.constraint: The value the option gives the form. Without the attribute, the label text with its white space collapsed, as in the native option.

secondary.constraint: The helper text after the label, already localized. Empty turns it off.

start.constraint: The start of the option. The same start for every option of a list. Any other value draws nothing and emits console.error in development.

icon.constraint: A core name of nph-icon, drawn with start=icon at icon/size-md. Any name outside the core draws nothing and emits console.error in development.

src.constraint: The photo of the avatar, with start=avatar. Empty shows the empty avatar.

status.constraint: The color of the dot, with start=dot: status/* or, for neutral, color/muted-foreground. Absent, the dot follows the text color (D6). Any other value draws nothing and emits console.error in development.

disabled.constraint: The option cannot be chosen and the keyboard skips it; the whole option at state/disabled-opacity.

selected.constraint: Written by the list that owns the option, never by the consumer: the chosen option. The list chooses by its own value. There is no selected attribute.

active.constraint: Written by the list that owns the option, never by the consumer: the option the pointer or the keyboard is on.

start.choose_when: icon when a symbol helps recognize the option; avatar when the options are people; dot when each option has a state; none in every other case.
do_not_combine_with: Options with and without a start in the same list.
A checkbox marker, which belongs to nph-multi-combobox.

default.changes_for_user: The label in color/popover-foreground on the list background, with no background of its own.

active.changes_for_user: The option the pointer or the keyboard is on: color/accent, with the text in color/accent-foreground (D5).

selected.changes_for_user: The chosen option: color/primary-surface and the check in color/primary. It wins over active (D5).

disabled.changes_for_user: The whole option at state/disabled-opacity; it cannot be chosen.

business_rules: The option never chooses itself: the list that owns it writes selected and active.
Without the value attribute, the value is the label text.
The selected background wins over the active one.

tokens.label: text/label-md in color/popover-foreground; color/accent-foreground when active
tokens.secondary: text/label-md in color/muted-foreground, space/inline-tight after the label
tokens.dot: space/inline square, radius/full, in an icon/size-md box; status/* or color/muted-foreground
tokens.selected: color/primary-surface with the check, icon/size-sm in color/primary

ai_hints: Write nph-option only as a child of the list that owns it, such as nph-select.
Give every option of a list the same start.
With start=dot, write the state in the label: the color only reinforces it.
Set value when the label is translated or may change; the form reads the value.
Never set selected or active by hand: set the value of the list.

accessibility.semantics: Role option through ElementInternals, with aria-selected and aria-disabled; it writes no ARIA attribute on its own host.
accessibility.accessible_name: The label text and the secondary text. The start, the dot and the check are hidden from the screen reader.
keyboard: not_applicable: the option never takes the focus; the list that owns it handles the keyboard.
accessibility.focus: not_applicable: the focus stays on the trigger of the list, which points to the active option with aria-activedescendant.
accessibility.contrast: The label meets 4.5:1 on color/popover, color/accent and color/primary-surface, in light and dark mode; the check on color/primary-surface measures 4.78:1 and 6.26:1 (D8).
accessibility.color_alternative: The selected option has the check besides the background; the dot goes with the written state.

invalid_combinations: A start outside none, icon, avatar and dot — the option draws nothing.
A status outside the six — the option draws nothing.
An icon outside the core names — the option draws nothing.
An option on its own, outside a list — it has no role there.
anti_patterns: Using the option on its own, outside a list.
Putting a checkbox on the option.
Mixing options with and without a start in the same list.
Using the status dot without a written state.
Setting selected or active by hand.
